## What the operator asked for

> "we want it to be saved as records somewhere so we can access it over time — we
> know in brief x with size L we took 45 minutes to hunt, 10 on architect, 20 on
> forger, 10 on sentinel and 10 on warden. this way we can know where the pain point
> of the system is and where to improve, and if a model is degraded or affecting the
> OS — cause i wanna measure models too, so i need something to measure on. which
> also tells me we need to save the model" — 2026-08-26

Restated as requirements, without implying how:

**R1.** A hunt's cost is retrievable **over time** — months later, not just in the
session that produced it.

**R2.** Cost is broken down **per phase / per agent**, not just as a hunt total. The
operator's example shape: `brief X, size L, 45m total — 10 architect, 20 forger, 10
sentinel, 10 warden`.

**R3.** The **model** each agent ran on is recorded, so a degraded or changed model
can be distinguished from a degraded process.

**R4.** The purpose is diagnosis: *where is the pain point, and where do we improve.*
A record that cannot answer that has not met the requirement.

**R5.** Records, **not a dashboard.** The operator killed the hook-host feature that
fed the old dashboard and does not want it back. Whether anything ever reads these
rows visually is a separate, later question.

**R6 (added 2026-08-26).** **Harness-agnostic and brief-keyed.** The operator's
direction is an independent Igris harness; nothing here may depend on one harness's
files, hooks or telemetry, and the record is keyed to the brief, not the session.

## Facts — measured 2026-08-26

### The tables

| table | rows | `duration_ms` populated | tokens populated | model column |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `agent_events` | 244 | **0** | **0** (all four columns) | **none** |
| `agent_metrics` | 275 | 48 (17%) | n/a | **none** |

Two timing tables exist. Neither is complete. **Neither has any way to record a
model.** 217 of `agent_metrics`' 275 rows are `agent='session'`; only ~53 are agents.
*(Filing-time counts, ~14:50 UTC. One more `/rest` session row landed at 15:01:12 UTC;
the table holds 276 rows as of 2026-08-26 22:02 UTC.)*

**Added 2026-08-26 (fresh session):** `agent_events` has a **7-day purge** —
`DELETE FROM agent_events WHERE created_at < datetime('now','-7 days')` — executed as
a side effect of **listing instances**: inside `handleInstanceList` (the
`igris_instance_list` MCP tool, `brain-mcp-server/src/tools/instances.ts:176`) and
inside HTTP `GET /api/instances` (`src/index.ts:472`). Rows from 2026-08-14 still
exist 12 days later only because `/boot` moved to the `igris session gather` verb
(FR-195) and nothing has called `igris_instance_list` since. One call wipes the
record. This is a landmine under R1 and must be removed, not worked around.
`agent_events` IS in the sync table list (`src/tools/sync.ts:240`). `agent_metrics`'
only real durations are 48 rows from **February 2026** (architect avg 2.8 min,
forger 5.0, sentinel 5.3, warden 1.6) — the last time anything measured agents.

### Field inventory against the operator's requested shape

```
brief_id, effort ("size L")   -> brief_status              EXISTS, populated
phase (PLANNING/BUILDING/...) -> agent_events.phase        EXISTS, populated
agent role                    -> agent_events.agent        EXISTS, populated
duration per agent            -> agent_events.duration_ms  EXISTS, always 0
tokens per agent              -> agent_events.*_tokens     EXISTS, always 0
MODEL per agent               -> nowhere                   DOES NOT EXIST
hunt total / rework rounds    -> not stored; derivable only if the above land
```

### Why nothing lands

`.claude/settings.json` wires five agent-lifecycle events over HTTP:

| events | transport | target |
|---|---|---|
| `Stop`, `SubagentStart`, `SubagentStop`, `TaskCompleted`, `TeammateIdle` | http | `http://localhost:3001/api/hooks/event?project=igris-ai` |

Measured: `curl` returns **HTTP 000, connection refused.** Nothing listens on 3001.

Every `command` hook in the same file works — they exec scripts under
`$HOME/.igris/core/hooks/shared/`. Only the HTTP ones are dead.

**Precise, because the obvious reading is wrong:** the receiver is not missing from
the codebase. `brain-mcp-server/src/index.ts:1052` still registers
`app.post('/api/hooks/event', …)` (FR-088). What is absent is anything *serving* it
locally — the brain runs here as **stdio MCP processes** and only speaks HTTP as the
remote `https://brain.fifty.dev`. Port 3001 was the old local/VPS HTTP brain, and
the operator states that host feature was killed along with the old dashboard.

**`FR-089` ("SubagentStop Hook — Auto Agent Metrics via agent_type Field") is marked
Done** and shipped that wiring. A Done brief left five hooks posting into a void, and
nothing noticed for months. That is the "reports success without having checked"
class (L-1248): the hook fires, exits 0, and no row appears.

### What DOES work, stated as a fact rather than a recommendation

`igris_agent_event` lands rows — all 244 of them are its. The orchestrator calls it
at every phase transition. At the stop event the orchestrator holds `duration_ms`,
token counts (both arrive in the task-notification payload) and the model it selected
when spawning the agent. **None of the three is passed today, and the tool has no
model parameter.**

### Three blind spots

1. **Resumed agents emit nothing.** Continuing an agent via `SendMessage` produces no
   event — used ~8 times in the 2026-08-26 session. Invocation counts therefore
   UNDERCOUNT, concentrated in review rounds.
2. **Token cost is never persisted** anywhere, despite arriving with every agent.
3. **No hunt-level record exists.** Answering "how long did TD-420 take" required
   joining MIN/MAX of `agent_events.created_at`, which brackets orchestrator time
   rather than agent runtime.

## Open questions — as filed (answered under *Direction*)

1. **What is the record's grain?** Per agent invocation, per phase, per hunt, or
   several?
2. **Where do records live?** A new table, an existing one, an append-only log, or
   outside the brain DB entirely.
3. **What carries the data?** The hook path, the MCP-tool path, the orchestrator, or
   something else. FR-089 demonstrates that a carrier can be wired and silent.
4. **How is the model captured reliably?** Requested vs resolved.
5. **What happens to the five dead HTTP hooks?**
6. **What happens to the two-table split?**
7. **What is the retention horizon?**
8. **Does this need to survive a machine change or a brain rebuild?**

## Acceptance criteria — what any solution must satisfy (outcomes only)

- [x] A query answers the operator's question directly for a REAL hunt: brief, size,
      total, and minutes per phase — with the query and its output recorded
- [x] The model each agent ran on is retrievable, and the same agent role is
      comparable across two different models
- [x] Duration is non-zero for a real invocation, verified by reading the stored
      record — **not** by observing a carrier exit 0, which is the exact failure
      FR-089 shipped. Tokens are recorded when the harness exposes them and are
      explicitly NULL (not 0) when it does not
- [x] Work done by a RESUMED agent is represented as its own round; today it is
      invisible
- [x] The records survive the session that produced them and remain queryable
      months later — the 7-day purge is removed from every call site, shown by a
      test that lists instances and then still finds a 30-day-old row, and the
      retention decision is written down
- [x] Emission is enforced by a control that can fail, not by prose: a hunt whose
      brief lacks a start/stop pair for a phase in its Agent Log cannot be closed
      without the named escape hatch, and the gate is shown firing on a real
      omission (red first)
- [x] The five dead HTTP hooks are removed; `agent_metrics` is no longer written or
      read by any surface
- [x] Nothing shipped depends on a single harness's files, hooks or telemetry (R6)
- [x] Every number under *Corrected measurements* is classified: reproducible from
      the shipped record going forward, or one-time archaeology named as such

## Corrected measurements — fresh session 2026-08-26

Source: a one-time reconstruction from harness transcripts (Jul 27 → Aug 26; 1,119
invocation segments across 4 projects, 62 igris-ai hunts, 432 invocations), validated
by reproducing the three per-phase totals above exactly. The tooling was deliberately
NOT kept (claude-only; R6). These are **archaeology, not re-derivable** from what
ships — the record starts at ship time.

**1. The slowdown is the model's behaviour, not the harness and not the architecture.**

| agent | opus-4-8 (Jul 2–3, n=6) | opus-5 (n=968) | fable-5 (n=75) |
|---|---|---|---|
| architect | 5.4 min · 22 tool calls | 11.4 · 54 | 7.8 · 36 |
| forger | 15.6 · 63 | 22.3 · 85 | 33.1 · 189 |
| sentinel | 3.1 · 16 | 16.9 · 60 | 3.3 · 30 |
| warden | 3.2 · 18 | 6.6 · 36 | 4.6 · 37 |
| tool calls per active minute | 3.9–5.2 | 3.5–5.2 | 4.7–7.0 |

- Per-action speed is flat across the three models and across every Claude Code
  version 2.1.198 → 2.1.246. opus-5 does 2–4× more actions per invocation under an
  unchanged prompt (`sentinel.md` is the same 158 lines since Jul 1).
- Corroboration: Feb `agent_metrics` averages (2.8 / 5.0 / 5.3 / 1.6 min); and the
  best week on record — Jun 29–Jul 5, **after** the v7 cutover, on opus-4-8 — closed
  191 briefs (59 in igris-ai). Then a three-week gap, then opus-5 from Jul 27 at
  13–23/week.
- `f578dd2` had no effect on per-hunt cost: opus-5 hunts median active 112.5 min
  before (n=40) vs 112.0 after (n=12); invocations 6.0 → 5.5; resumed rounds 1.0 → 0.
  The "invocations tripled" finding was a baseline artefact (L-1401).
- Caveat: the opus-4-8 sample is 6 invocations (mbrgea-ai). The uncomfortable reading
  stays open: the prompts ask for mutation batteries and red-first proof, and opus-5
  may be the first model actually doing them. Whether the extra work catches defects
  is unmeasurable today — the reason this brief exists.

**2. The rest of the drop is not the model.** igris-ai Done per active day: May 6.2 /
Jun 5.2 / Aug 3.9 (−30%); active days 21 → 17; XS+S share of Done briefs 60% → 38%;
igris-ai's share of weekly agent capacity 60% → 25–50% (total capacity flat at ~4,000
active agent-min/week across projects).

**3. Where hunt time goes:** forger 57%, sentinel 27%, warden 11%, architect 6%;
resumed rounds 14%. Hunt wall-clock median 145 min, p75 270; 19 of 62 hunts > 4 h —
since late July, not since Aug 14.

**4. Review has a floor (TD-425, quantified).** opus-5 hunts by forger-minute third:
forger 29 / 67 / 119 → sentinel 23 / 30 / 45.5, warden 11 / 12.5 / 18.5.

**5. The existing carrier is accurate but uncontrolled.** When emitted, the
brain-timestamped start→stop bracket overshoots real agent time by 0.9–2.1 min on
TD-420's five pairs (sentinel 40.5/18.6/15.9 vs 39.1/16.5/14.9; warden 13.9/5.9 vs
12.8/5.0); on FR-267's own eleven pairs the excess is 1.0–6.2 min, median 2.2 (doc §7
table) — it is orchestrator wait between the agent's return and its stop event and is
not bounded (warden r1's 6.2 = the orchestrator mid-investigation when the review
returned). But since Aug 14 only **35 of 112** real invocations got a start event
(31%); **8 of 18 hunts have zero events**; 10 starts never stopped, 18 stops never
started. Prose emission is not a control (L-1314).

**6. Harness transcripts hold everything R1–R4 ask for** (model, active time, tokens,
resumes; 30-day TTL) — recorded as L-1404 and **rejected** as source and as audit:
claude-only, contrary to R6.

## Direction — decided 2026-08-26

The carrier stays the orchestrator (the only actor present on every harness, and the
thing a future Igris harness will be). What changes is that the record becomes
**brain-timed, complete, and enforced** — the schema was never the problem; the
control was.

| # | question | decision | rejected |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | grain | **per invocation** (one start/stop pair = one row), with a `round` index so a resume is its own row. Per-phase and per-hunt are **derived**, never stored | storing hunt totals (would drift from the rows) |
| 2 | where | **evolve `agent_events`**: add `model_requested` (NOT NULL), `model_resolved` (NULL), `round` (default 1); tokens stay, NULL when unknown. A brief-keyed `hunt_runs` view derives R2's shape. **Remove the 7-day purge from both call sites** | new table (loses 12 days of rows and the sync wiring for no gain); outside the brain (R1, R8) |
| 3 | carrier | orchestrator → `igris_agent_event` (or a CLI verb with the same contract), **duration computed by the brain from its own start/stop timestamps** — never trusted from the caller. Harness telemetry (tokens, resolved model) = optional enrichment on stop | harness hooks (single-harness; FR-089 proved silent); transcript extraction (single-harness; R6) |
| 4 | model | `model_requested` is mandatory (the orchestrator chose it — pass it); `model_resolved` recorded when the harness reports it. Requested meets R3 now; resolved is the future harness's job | inferring the model after the fact |
| 5 | dead hooks | **remove** the five HTTP hooks from the projected settings; a carrier that exits 0 and lands nothing is L-1248 in config form | repair (nothing should listen on 3001 again) |
| 6 | two tables | consolidate on `agent_events`; `agent_metrics` stops being written and read (the 48 Feb rows stay as history) | migrating Feb rows into agent_events |
| 7 | retention | durable: no purge on `agent_events`; `event_log` stays 30-day ephemeral | — |
| 8 | survive machine/brain change | yes — `agent_events` is already in the sync table list; the plan verifies the push actually carries it (suggestion #1549: push may skip rows silently) | — |

**Enforcement (the part that was missing):** extend the `commit-msg` gate that owns
`IGRIS_BYPASS_AC_GATE` (contract: `core/enforcement/brief-ac-completion.md`) so a
`closes #X` commit is **refused** when X's Agent Log phases lack a matching start/stop
pair — escape hatch `IGRIS_BYPASS_EVENT_GATE=1`, one-shot, same convention as the
others. *Refuse rather than warn* — **confirmed by the operator 2026-08-26 at plan
approval.** Red-first: the gate is demonstrated on a real omitted event before it
is trusted.

**Scope split:** hunt cost is this brief. The OS-wide numbers the operator also asked
for (capacity by project, Done/week, ceremony cost, effort mix, model per role) are
**FR-268**, which depends on this record and reuses the same start/stop contract.

**Experiments this unlocks (not in scope here):** model-per-role — sentinel is 27% of
hunt time and its extra ~44 tool calls per run vs opus-4-8 is the largest single line;
TD-425's proportionate review; and the honest test of whether opus-5's extra work
catches defects.

**Plan-time checks:** (a) delete the purge from `handleInstanceList` AND
`GET /api/instances`, with a regression test; (b) `agent_events` rows actually arrive
on the remote after a push; (c) every `igris_agent_event` call site in `/hunt` passes
`model_requested` and `round`; (d) `IGRIS_BYPASS_*` never exported; (e) the gate
reads the Agent Log phases from the brief content, so a hunt that skipped a phase
legitimately (e.g. no architect on an S brief) is not blocked for it.

**Plan approval (2026-08-26):** architect re-rated M → L (38 files, 7 phases; plan at
`~/.igris/projects/igris-ai/plans/FR-267-plan.md`). Operator approved **Option A —
full scope** (including retiring the three `igris_metrics_*` read tools and the VPS
deploy-before-push) and **refuse** mode for the gate. Two plan deviations accepted:
`model_requested` is NULLABLE at the DDL (SQLite `ADD COLUMN … NOT NULL` needs a
default; a sentinel would violate the NULL-not-fake rule) and enforced at the gateway
+ handler instead; a fourth column `project` is added so the record is brief-keyed
(`instances` rows are deleted on `/rest`, so the join cannot happen at read time).
